\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹرالی} (ṭrālī)}{ٹرالی (ṭrālī)}]{\ur{ٹرالی} (ṭrālī) — a luggage trolley}

\label{lesson:UR-C401-trali}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to spend (time), then the Urdu for a return.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹرالی}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹرالی}} — \emph{ṭrālī} — \textquotedblleft{}a luggage trolley\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{اپنا} \ur{سامان} \ur{ٹرالی} \ur{پر} \ur{رکھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne apnā sāmān ṭrālī par rakhā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I put my luggage on a trolley.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹرالی}} (\emph{ṭrālī}) is borrowed from English \emph{trolley}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭrālī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭrālī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maiṅ ne apnā sāmān ṭrālī par rakhā.} — I put my luggage on a trolley.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to spend (time), then the Urdu for a return, then say \emph{ṭrālī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ٹرالی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A luggage trolley\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منتظر} (muntazir)}{منتظر (muntazir)}]{\ur{منتظر} (muntazir) — waiting (for someone)}

\label{lesson:UR-C401-muntazir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a return, then the Urdu for a luggage trolley.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منتظر}}
\textbf{\ur{منتظر}} — \emph{muntazir} — \textquotedblleft{}waiting (for someone)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہمارا} \ur{دوست} \ur{باہر} \ur{ہمارا} \ur{منتظر} \ur{تھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hamārā dost bāhar hamārā muntazir thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our friend was outside, waiting for us.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منتظر}} (\emph{muntazir}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muntaẓir}, \textquotedblleft{}one who waits\textquotedblright{}; it is a cousin of \textbf{\ur{انتظار}}, \textquotedblleft{}waiting\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muntazir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hamārā dost bāhar hamārā muntazir thā.} — Our friend was outside, waiting for us.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a return, then the Urdu for a luggage trolley, then say \emph{muntazir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{استقبال} (istiqbāl)}{استقبال (istiqbāl)}]{\ur{استقبال} (istiqbāl) — a welcome; a reception}

\label{lesson:UR-C401-istiqbal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a luggage trolley, then the Urdu for waiting (for someone).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{استقبال}}
\textbf{\ur{استقبال}} — \emph{istiqbāl} — \textquotedblleft{}a welcome; a reception\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دوستوں} \ur{نے} \ur{پھولوں} \ur{سے} \ur{ہمارا} \ur{استقبال} \ur{کیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dostoṅ ne phūloṅ se hamārā istiqbāl kiyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our friends welcomed us with flowers.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{استقبال}} (\emph{istiqbāl}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{istiqbāl}, \textquotedblleft{}going out to meet, receiving\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\ur{استقبال} \ur{کرنا}} is to welcome someone.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istiqbāl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dostoṅ ne phūloṅ se hamārā istiqbāl kiyā.} — Our friends welcomed us with flowers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a luggage trolley, then the Urdu for waiting (for someone), then say \emph{istiqbāl} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گلدستہ} (guldastā)}{گلدستہ (guldastā)}]{\ur{گلدستہ} (guldastā) — a bouquet}

\label{lesson:UR-C401-guldasta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for waiting (for someone), then the Urdu for a welcome.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{گلدستہ}}
\textbf{\ur{گلدستہ}} — \emph{guldastā} — \textquotedblleft{}a bouquet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سارا} \ur{نے} \ur{اپنی} \ur{بہن} \ur{کو} \ur{گلدستہ} \ur{دیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sārā ne apnī bahan ko guldastā diyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Sara gave her sister a bouquet.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{گلدستہ}} (\emph{guldastā}) is built from Persian \emph{gul}, \textquotedblleft{}a flower\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{dasta}, \textquotedblleft{}a handful\textquotedblright{}: it is usually traced to Persian \emph{guldasta}, \textquotedblleft{}a bunch of flowers\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{guldastā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{guldastā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sārā ne apnī bahan ko guldastā diyā.} — Sara gave her sister a bouquet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for waiting (for someone), then the Urdu for a welcome, then say \emph{guldastā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہلانا} (hilānā)}{ہلانا (hilānā)}]{\ur{ہلانا} (hilānā) — to wave; to shake}

\label{lesson:UR-C401-hilana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a welcome, then the Urdu for a bouquet.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہلانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ہلانا}} — \emph{hilānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to wave; to shake\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دوستوں} \ur{نے} \ur{ہمیں} \ur{دیکھ} \ur{کر} \ur{ہاتھ} \ur{ہلائے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dostoṅ ne hameṅ dekh kar hāth hilāe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our friends saw us and waved.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{ہاتھ} \ur{ہلایا}, \emph{us ne hāth hilāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہلانا}} (\emph{hilānā}) is built on \emph{hilnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to shake\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under \emph{hillati}, \textquotedblleft{}moves, shakes\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 14120): this is the form for shaking something.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hilānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hilānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dostoṅ ne hameṅ dekh kar hāth hilāe.} — Our friends saw us and waved.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a welcome, then the Urdu for a bouquet, then say \emph{hilānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ہلانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To wave; to shake\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Potholes and Jolts to Meeting the Plane}

\label{lesson:UR-R401-review-394-401}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for a pothole and a driver.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a pothole, a driver, a shove, to bounce, deserted
  \item a tyre, a puncture, a collision, a helmet, to get dented
  \item a highway, a toll, a checkpoint (on a road), a convoy, to drive (animals or a cart)
  \item a distance, a kilometre, a mountain pass, to turn (something), to show (someone) around
  \item a flight, an aircraft, a seat (formal), to tighten, postponed
  \item protection, a security search, customs (at a border), forbidden, to put on board
  \item a homeland, a foreign land, a stranger, to spend (time), a return
  \item a luggage trolley, waiting (for someone), a welcome, a bouquet, to wave
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A pothole? (\textbf{\ur{گڑھا}}, \emph{gaṛhā}.) A driver? (\textbf{\ur{ڈرائیور}}, \emph{ḍrāivar}.) A shove? (\textbf{\ur{دھکا}}, \emph{dhakkā}.) To bounce? (\textbf{\ur{اچھلنا}}, \emph{uchhalnā}.) Deserted? (\textbf{\ur{ویران}}, \emph{vīrān}.) A tyre? (\textbf{\ur{ٹائر}}, \emph{ṭāyar}.) A puncture? (\textbf{\ur{پنکچر}}, \emph{pankchar}.) A collision? (\textbf{\ur{ٹکر}}, \emph{ṭakkar}.) A helmet? (\textbf{\ur{ہیلمٹ}}, \emph{helmeṭ}.) To get dented? (\textbf{\ur{پچکنا}}, \emph{pichaknā}.) A highway? (\textbf{\ur{شاہراہ}}, \emph{shāhrāh}.) A toll? (\textbf{\ur{محصول}}, \emph{mahsūl}.) A checkpoint (on a road)? (\textbf{\ur{ناکہ}}, \emph{nākā}.) A convoy? (\textbf{\ur{قافلہ}}, \emph{qāfilā}.) To drive (animals or a cart)? (\textbf{\ur{ہانکنا}}, \emph{hāṅknā}.) A distance? (\textbf{\ur{فاصلہ}}, \emph{fāslā}.) A kilometre? (\textbf{\ur{کلومیٹر}}, \emph{kilomīṭar}.) A mountain pass? (\textbf{\ur{درہ}}, \emph{darrā}.) To turn (something)? (\textbf{\ur{موڑنا}}, \emph{moṛnā}.) To show (someone) around? (\textbf{\ur{گھمانا}}, \emph{ghumānā}.) A flight? (\textbf{\ur{پرواز}}, \emph{parvāz}.) An aircraft? (\textbf{\ur{طیارہ}}, \emph{tayyārā}.) A seat (formal)? (\textbf{\ur{نشست}}, \emph{nashist}.) To tighten? (\textbf{\ur{کسنا}}, \emph{kasnā}.) Postponed? (\textbf{\ur{ملتوی}}, \emph{multavī}.) Protection? (\textbf{\ur{حفاظت}}, \emph{hifāzat}.) A security search? (\textbf{\ur{تلاشی}}, \emph{talāshī}.) Customs (at a border)? (\textbf{\ur{کسٹم}}, \emph{kasṭam}.) Forbidden? (\textbf{\ur{ممنوع}}, \emph{mamnū}.) To put on board? (\textbf{\ur{چڑھانا}}, \emph{chaṛhānā}.) A homeland? (\textbf{\ur{وطن}}, \emph{vatan}.) A foreign land? (\textbf{\ur{پردیس}}, \emph{pardes}.) A stranger? (\textbf{\ur{اجنبی}}, \emph{ajnabī}.) To spend (time)? (\textbf{\ur{گزارنا}}, \emph{guzārnā}.) A return? (\textbf{\ur{واپسی}}, \emph{vāpasī}.) A luggage trolley? (\textbf{\ur{ٹرالی}}, \emph{ṭrālī}.) Waiting (for someone)? (\textbf{\ur{منتظر}}, \emph{muntazir}.) A welcome? (\textbf{\ur{استقبال}}, \emph{istiqbāl}.) A bouquet? (\textbf{\ur{گلدستہ}}, \emph{guldastā}.) To wave? (\textbf{\ur{ہلانا}}, \emph{hilānā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
